title: Reflection debuts Beam, an open-weight AI model to rival Chinese models at lower compute cost
source_used: TechCrunch (Rebecca Bellan), 5 Oct 2026, read from fulltext/C01-01.txt (HTTP 200)
key_facts: Reflection AI, a Brooklyn startup founded in 2024 by two former Google DeepMind researchers, officially unveiled Beam, its first frontier open-weight model, in a blog post on Monday 5 Oct 2026.

Beam is a text-only mixture-of-experts model: 501 billion parameters, 23 billion active, pretrained on 23.8 trillion tokens, 1 million token context window; Z.ai's GLM-5.2 has about 744 billion total and 40 billion active.

The company says Beam scores on par with Z.ai's GLM-5.2 on advanced reasoning benchmarks and beats today's leading Western open models with '3-4x less inference compute'; the claims have not been independently verified.
Reflection's own benchmarks show Beam beating Thinking Machines Lab's Inkling (released in July) on four coding tests where both report results; Inkling is multimodal, Beam is text-only.
Reflection says it will release Beam's weights and full technical details this month, with distribution through hyperscalers and neoclouds and open-source library integrations at launch.

Reflection has raised about $4.7 billion per PitchBook (backers include Nvidia, Sequoia Capital, Lightspeed), was last valued at $25 billion pre-money, and signed compute deals worth over $7 billion with SpaceX and Nebius for Nvidia GB300 chips through 2029.

It pitches Beam to enterprises and sovereign nations for 'AI factories' (customised local AI systems trained on an institution's own data) and is testing a sovereign AI factory partnership with Shinsegae Group in South Korea.
The announcement confirms Axios's weekend reporting that Reflection was close to a launch; Reflection did not answer TechCrunch's requests in time.
quote_evidence: Reflection AI is officially unveiling Beam, its first frontier, open-weight AI model.

Reflection’s performance claims haven’t been independently verified, but on advanced reasoning benchmarks, the company says Beam scores on par with Z.ai’s GLM-5.2 and outperforms today’s leading Western open models while using “3-4x less inference compute.”
Reflection says it will release Beam’s weights and full technical details this month, with distribution through hyperscalers and neoclouds and integrations across open source libraries at launch.
why_it_matters_hint: It could heat up the race for a Western open-weight alternative to DeepSeek, Qwen and Z.ai, if Reflection's unverified claims hold.
event_date: 5 Oct 2026 (Reflection's blog post, a Monday); the earlier Axios scoop it confirms was published 4 Oct 2026.
notes: Follow-up of item 63 in our 5 Oct 2026 edition (Axios scoop of 4 Oct 2026). New today: the name Beam, its size, Reflection's own benchmark claims and a promise to publish the weights this month. 'Open-weight' is still a promise: the weights are not public yet. Status PRELIMINARY because the performance claims are the company's own and unverified; the unveiling itself is official. TechCrunch does not say exactly whom the '3-4x less inference compute' is measured against (an earlier line says 'of rivals'), so the summary says 'rival models'.
